::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Gabriel's horn about the y-axis](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/713755/gabriels-horn-about-the-y-axis), asked by [user3407266](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/134727/user3407266) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2014-03-15; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I'm trying to figure out if there is a solution to finding the volume of the shape that is formed by rotating $f(x) = \frac 1x$ about the y-axis. Not the x-axis as in Gabriel's horn, but the same problem about the y-axis on the interval $x \ge 1$.
>
> Using the shell method and improper integrals, I end up with $\pi$($\infty$ - 1) where b $\to \infty$.
>
> Is the volume on this infinite? If so, what is the correct way to prove that it is infinite?
:::

OP wanted to use the shell method on this problem. user65203's comment is the right answer. The volume would be
$$\int_1^\infty 2\pi x \cdot \frac{1}{x} \,dx
    =\int_1^\infty 2\pi\,dx$$
and this diverges.
